question: How is an EFW2 wage file laid out, step by step, so the AccuWage test files make sense?

takeaways.text: A wage file is a stack of lines that are each exactly 512 bytes, and the first two letters of a line say whether it is the submitter, an employer, one W-2, an employer's totals, or the end.
takeaways.because: the reader asked to understand the format easily, and the line order is what every file shares

takeaways.text: Each W-2 box sits at fixed byte positions, and money is whole cents padded with zeros on the left, so 52000.00 dollars is written 00005200000.
takeaways.because: AccuWage finds values by position, which is the part a reader of the raw text cannot see

takeaways.text: Each employer's totals line must equal the sum of its W-2 lines and the final line counts every W-2, and the broken test files each break one of these rules on purpose.
takeaways.because: files 94, 95 and 97 only make sense once the totals and the length rule are clear

claims.text: the user asked for a stepping drawing that makes the wage file format easy to understand
a file is RA, then per employer an RE, its RW lines and an RT, then one RF

evidence.quote: RA, then each employer's RE, RW rows, and RT, then RF

claims.text: every record is built in a 512-character buffer and the validator flags any line of another length
SSA's format has no labels or separators inside a line, so the length is the only thing that keeps every field at its position

rejected.fails: SSA accepts only EFW2, which Pub 42-007 defines as exact 512-byte records

evidence.quote: The record length must be exactly 512 bytes.

claims.text: money is written as whole cents with zeros added on the left until the field is full; text is padded with spaces on the right
whole cents need no decimal point, and adding cents never rounds, so the totals line can match the W-2 lines to the cent

rejected.fails: the point takes a byte and fractional dollars round, so a total could drift by a cent

claims.text: while it writes each W-2 line the writer adds its cents into the employer's totals, then writes RT, and RF gets the count of all W-2 lines
SSA checks that RT holds the total of the RW lines since the last RE, and calls a mismatch out of balance

rejected.option: leaving the totals for SSA to add up
rejected.fails: Pub 42-007 requires RT, and a wrong RT is the out-of-balance error file 94 tests

evidence.quote: Enter the total for all RW (Employee) Records reported since the last RE (Employer) Record

claims.text: file 01 has 7 records in the order RA RE RW RW RW RT RF, each 512 bytes

evidence.quote: file 01: 7 records: RA RE RW RW RW RT RF · each 512 bytes + CR LF

claims.text: the RW line splits into type 2, SSN 9, name 50, address and more 126, box 1 11, box 2 11, boxes 3-6 44, the rest 259

evidence.quote: RW layout widths: type 2 · SSN 9 · name 50 · address and more 126 · box 1 11 · box 2 11 · boxes 3-6 44 · the rest 259 = 512

claims.text: Maria's box 1 wages 52000.00 are 5200000 cents and are written 00005200000 at RW 188-198
file 94's RW wages add to 321400.25 and RT says 321500.25; file 95's RF says 4 with 3 RW lines; file 97 has one 511-byte RW line

evidence.quote: file 94: RW wages sum 321400.25 · RT 10-24 says 321500.25 · off by 100.00

claims.text: file 94 puts 100.00 too much in RT, an out-of-balance error
file 95's RF claims 4 W-2 lines and the file has 3

evidence.quote: RF Number of RW Records says 4; the file has 3.

claims.text: file 97 has one W-2 line of 511 bytes, a critical error that stops testing
